correctness.rationale: For the fully specified Chvátal graph, face and induced-degree definitions are checked on all 4,095 nonempty vertex subsets. Exactly 424 faces, an explicit 211-pair acyclic Forman matching and the exhaustive 1,428-cover Hasse topological sort prove K≃S³ integrally; critical cells are one dimension-0 and one dimension-3. The four deletion/link models each have exhaustive matching certificates; L0 and D2 additionally have explicitly checked free-face simplicial collapses of 60 and 152 pairs. An exhaustive census of all eight automorphisms proves orbit completeness. A second independently encoded face enumeration and exact GF(2) boundary-rank calculation checks all five homologies; its signed permutation-Lefschetz calculation proves the D4 top-homology character with r↦−1,s↦+1. This does not claim a strict equivariant sphere model.

originality.rationale: The first higher-independence results cited address complete multipartite graphs, cycles, whiskered graphs or trees, whereas the cyclic four-regular Chvátal graph lies outside their hypotheses. The directly overlapping publicly recorded Chvátal statements classify ordinary Ind1 and the ordinary open-neighborhood complex and determine a DIFFERENT, opposite deletion/link orbit pattern and degree-two orientation character. Full public result statements were retrieved, their exact definitions and deductions compared, and none implies the new Ind2 statement, relative inclusions or degree-three character. Targeted exact, alias and semantic searches of the mathematical record returned no equivalent or stronger Chvátal Ind2 assertion. An unindexed or unpublished prior statement remains possible.
residual_risks: Semantic search and accessible indexed public records cannot rule out independent unindexed or unpublished calculations of the identical two-independence complex.
No general theorem covering every triangle-free four-chromatic graph was identified; discovery is not an exhaustive proof against all possible broader theorems.
The original 1970 graph construction note is used only for provenance, not claimed fully inspected for topological results.

value.rationale: The graph is the canonical smallest four-regular triangle-free four-chromatic example. The second-independence question changes the forbidden induced structures from edges to paths on three vertices. For this natural extremal graph that change raises a known S² to a newly computed S³ and provably REVERSES the full two-orbit deletion/link dichotomy relative to ordinary independence. Classifying canonical inclusions, simplicial collapsibility and the sign character for its entire D4 action supplies structural topology not captured by Betti numbers. The specific finite graph is mathematically motivated independently of its computed outcome and is a useful test case for path-free/higher-independence methods; no unjustified general family theorem is asserted.
